categories.name: tests
why: P3 because it improves failure diagnostics across many test files and is stated to partly unblock the boost-removal effort in #35713, but it adds no new test coverage and the benefit is developer convenience rather than catching regressions.
Bounded scope: author confirms conversion is exhaustive for types with new `<<` operators, leaving integer comparisons and some vector-of-vector cases as deliberate follow-up.

result.summary: This PR adds `operator<<` overloads for commonly-used Bitcoin Core test types (CService, CAddress, FeeFrac, key and address types, KeyOriginInfo, txindex::BlockTxPosition, etc.) in a new src/test/util/common.cpp/h, and converts many bare BOOST_CHECK equality checks across roughly a dozen test files to BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL/_NE so boost can print the mismatched values on failure. The author states the display strings are also intended for reuse in #35713 (removing boost as the unit test runner), though a reviewer notes only the first commit is strictly needed there. The PR does not migrate types that already have debug output, vector<T> comparisons, or types needing friend access, leaving those as explicit follow-up.
result.problem: Unit test failures using bare BOOST_CHECK on custom types currently print nothing useful (e.g. just a boolean false), making debugging test failures slower for contributors. This affects anyone triaging a failing unit test across many files (addrman, key, script, descriptor, mempool fee estimator, etc.).

resolved_concerns: jeanpablojp's concern about SIGABRT on invalid CExtKey/CExtPubKey printers was fixed with length/validity guards.
jeanpablojp's concern about missing fields (nTime, nServices, m_net) not reflected in printers vs operator== was fixed by adding those fields to the display strings.
maflcko/purpleKarrot's suggestions to de-templatize and move implementations to a .cpp file, and to generalize the std::pair printer, were applied.
ismaelsadeeq's request for more descriptive field labels and inclusion of a CScript printer were applied.
jeanpablojp's ScriptToAsmStr ambiguity concern (two different scripts printing identically) was addressed by adding hex alongside asm.
sedited's question about how exhaustive the BOOST_CHECK conversion is was answered with a documented regex sweep and further conversions plus an updated PR description.

result.card: This PR adds `operator<<` debug-output overloads for common Bitcoin Core test types (CService, CAddress, FeeFrac, key/address types, KeyOriginInfo, etc.) in a new test/util/common.{h,cpp}, and converts many bare BOOST_CHECK equality checks to BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL/_NE across roughly a dozen unit test files so failures print useful values instead of just pass/fail. It solves a real but modest developer-productivity problem: debugging failing unit tests currently gives little information for custom types. The author states the printers are also intended for reuse in the larger #35713 (removing boost as unit test runner), though a reviewer (ismaelsadeeq) notes only part of the change is strictly needed there. Review has been thorough and iterative across three weeks, with several substantive issues (SIGABRT risk on invalid keys, missing fields vs operator==, ambiguous script printing) found and fixed, ending in reACKs from ismaelsadeeq and jeanpablojp and an approval from maflcko. The PR is Ready for review now with strong agreement and no open objections.
